statements.subject: server
statements.description: The second use is for the bulk transfer of articles from one store to another... this process is called 'peering' or 'transit'.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The first use is 'reading', where the client fetches articles from a large store maintained by the server for immediate or later presentation to a user.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY provide different modes of behaviour (transit, reader, or a combination) to different client connections.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Except as an effect of the MODE READER command (Section 5.3) on a mode-switching server, once a server advertises either or both of the IHAVE or READER capabilities, it MUST continue to advertise them for the entire session.
actions: server changes advertised capabilities per MODE READER effect

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once a server advertises either or both of the IHAVE or READER capabilities, it MUST continue to advertise them for the entire session.
statements.guard_semantics: Once set to IHAVE or READER (or both), must remain set for session duration unless MODE READER command is issued on a mode-switching server
